feedback.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,2]\times [-i,0].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[0,2]\times [-0.5,0]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,2],b\in [-0.5,0]}.
$$

This represents a rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(2,0),$ $(2,-0.5),$ and $(0,-0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/5837864bfcc40e680cf62b43c0e3d145ba05b1f25e1ccae2f4788902d030d927.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,2]\times [-i,0]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [0,2],b\in [-i,0]}
$$

is the rectangle whose vertices are at $(0,0),$ $(2,0),$ $(2,-i),$ and $(0,-i).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/f0c20436f03db4b0003d087827cefbd76506af423da3f0a3042082b5afeb4b58.png)

The intersection of all these rectangles is the line segment $[0,2]\times {0}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/236d10f31265b400036e1ddeafa122991bcae1ea878af8b300003fb11acfa85b.png)
